A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STRAP and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite additions, removals, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on three streaming datasets with four backbones, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and distribution-shift case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds key-component ablations, data-constrained evaluations, retrieval-method comparisons, and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same subgraph construction, three pattern libraries, key/value generation, similarity retrieval, and fusion procedure. The new component ablations test existing features rather than introduce method components.

E1.justification: The same three datasets and forecasting tasks remain. Section 5.4 adds conditions described as both few-shot learning and 30%/50% missing data, but does not explain whether these involve only reduced training samples or missing inputs. This prevents reliably distinguishing an E3-only sample-size change from distinct input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6.1 and Figure 9 add evaluated comparisons with RAGraph and PRODIGY on ENERGY-Stream across all four backbones. This substantially strengthens direct comparison with related graph-learning approaches beyond the existing comparator suite, which remains in the original benchmark tables.

E3.justification: Table 2 introduces 30% and 50% missing-data conditions, while Figure 10 introduces an ASTGNN/ENERGY-Stream comparison of MAPE against reciprocal training time per epoch. The original 6/2/2 split and forecasting metrics remain; Table 7 discloses settings rather than establishes changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds ablations of six spatial and temporal key-feature groups, retains the previous TGCN library ablation, and removes the STGNN library-ablation panel. Section 5.4 and Appendix C.6.2 also add data-availability and computational-cost analyses, substantially expanding diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three different random seeds and report average performance, with unchanged uncertainty entries in retained tables. New table entries and Figure 9 error bars do not establish a changed repetition count or statistical estimation practice.

E6.justification: The original benchmark tables are numerically unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results in Table 2 and Figures 2, 9, and 10. Examples include reported average MAE of 6.29 and 5.77 under 50% and 30% missing data, and MAPE of 49.97 after removing spatial key group S3. The earlier STGNN library-ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, method equations, graph-construction formula, and Theorem B.1 with its proof are retained. No substantive change to assumptions, derivations, or formal guarantees is present.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about plug-and-play pattern retrieval, adaptive fusion, reduced forgetting, and STOOD generalization. The added experiments do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets geometric curvature and statistical/spectral descriptors as particularly important, with wavelet features less critical in the tested setting. Appendix C.6 explains library-maintenance and retrieval costs and argues for an accuracy–efficiency tradeoff. The original historical-data and library-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Table 7 specifies learning rates by method and dataset and batch size 128, refining v1's general statement that learning rates are 0.03 or 0.01. Hardware reporting remains unchanged. Removing Appendix E also removes explicit public-data and anonymization disclosures, without establishing any actual change in data access.

R1.justification: v3 adds 13 references, including RAGraph, PRODIGY, and additional graph/time-series research, while retaining the earlier references. The related-work narrative remains largely unchanged, with limited additional positioning through the new comparator discussion.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the ablation discussion, added research questions and Sections 5.4/C.6, updated affiliations and conference header, and removal of the broader-impact and data-ethics appendices. Most introductory, methodological, theoretical, and concluding prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2 and 7 and Figures 9 and 10. Figure 2 changes from two backbone-specific library-ablation panels to library/key panels, and Figure 3 is redrawn with probability-density axes and training/testing legends. These substantially expand and revise the empirical displays.

improvement.justification: The new ablations, direct comparisons, timing analysis, and explicit hyperparameters improve scrutiny of STRAP. However, new Table 2 is labeled TGCN while its full-data STRAP results, MAE 4.85 and MAPE 43.11, match STGNN Table 1 rather than TGCN Table 4's 4.98 and 43.65. Missing-data construction is also unspecified. These unresolved reporting and protocol issues make the reliability of important added evidence unclear, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
